newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt may slow car tariff cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt may slow car tariff cuts - paper.

text.p: Australia's national government may heed the pleas of the country's anxious car industry by freezing tariff cuts and reducing wholesale sales tax, the Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Friday.

Under the plan passenger motor vehicle tariffs would remain at 15 percent from 2000 until 2005, instead of phased down to five percent as proposed by the government's Productivity Commission. Wholesale sales tax on cars would be cut from its current level of 22 percent, effectively reducing the price of imported and locally produced vehicles by about 10 percent.

The commission's recommendations, in a draft report released in December, prompted warnings from car makers that they could pull out of Australia. General Motors Corp, Ford Motor Co, Toyota Motor Corp and Mitsubishi Motors Corp have manufacturing operations in Australia.
The Department of Industry, Science and Technology may support the plan, but some officials said it preferred a differential system of tariffs instead of tax cuts, the paper said.
The Treasury, also discussing future protection for the industry, may put up some resistence to the plan, favouring the application of market forces in the car industry, the paper said.
The government has yet to decide its formal response to the commission's recommendations.
A final commission report is due next week, after industry consultation.
